items.topic: sampling-t2 · unbiasedness and variance of stratified and simple-random-sampling means
items.stem: A population of size N is divided into L strata of sizes N₁,…,N_L. A stratified random sample of size n is drawn, with n_j units selected by simple random sampling within stratum j. Let ȳ_j be the sample mean in stratum j and define ȳ_st=∑_{j=1}^L(N_j/N)ȳ_j. An independent simple random sample of size n is also drawn from the population, with sample mean ȳ and variance of the sample mean σ². Which statements are correct?
statements: ȳ_st is an unbiased estimator of the population mean.
ȳ is an unbiased estimator of the population mean.
The variance σ²_st of ȳ_st is always less than or equal to σ².
If n_j/N_j=n/N for every stratum j, then σ²_st=σ².

A.why: Each stratum sample mean is design-unbiased for its stratum population mean, so their population-weighted sum is unbiased. The ordinary SRS sample mean is also unbiased.

B.why: Under simple random sampling, the sample mean is design-unbiased for the population mean.

C.why: Proportional allocation does not generally make the two variances equal. The stratified variance depends on within-stratum variation, while SRS variance also reflects between-stratum variation.

D.why: Statements 3 and 4 are not universal identities; proportional allocation alone does not imply equal variances.

items.explanation: For each stratum j, simple random sampling within that stratum gives E(ȳ_j)=Ȳ_j, the stratum population mean. Therefore E(ȳ_st)=∑(N_j/N)Ȳ_j=Ȳ, so statement 1 is true. An ordinary simple random sample mean is also unbiased for the population mean, so statement 2 is true. The variance of a stratified estimator is not always smaller than the SRS variance: the allocation across strata matters, and an inefficient allocation can increase variance. Thus statement 3 is false as a universal claim. Under proportional allocation, n_j/N_j=n/N, the variance expression still involves the within-stratum variances. The SRS variance involves the overall population variance, which includes both within- and between-stratum components. They are not generally equal, so statement 4 is false. Hence only statements 1 and 2 are correct. Other-exam relevance: stratified sampling, unbiasedness and design variance are relevant to UGC NET/JRF Statistics, GATE Statistics and State SET Statistics syllabi; This is topic overlap, not a claim that this exact question appeared in those other examinations.
